Order 
Thi s is first application filed by the applicant under Section 483 of BNSS, 2023/439 of the Cr.P.C.,
1973 for grant of regular bail relating to FIR No.89/2025, dated 14.02.2025, registered at Police Station- Pali, District - Umaria (M.P.) for commission of offence punishable under Section 376(2)
(N) of IPC.

Applicant is in detention since 20.02.2025.
2 .
As per the prosecution story, on 14.02.2025, 24 year old prosecutrix lodged FIR stating that her sister's marriage has been solemnized with Daduram Singh.
Her marriage was settled with the present applicant.
It is alleged that on 26.06.2023 and thereafter applicant repeatedly established physical relations by making false promise of marriage.
Now she has come to know that his marriage has been fixed with somewhere else and he has refused to enter into wedlock with her.
FIR was registered.

3. Learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that applicant has NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-JBP:17279 2 MCRC-11885-2025 not committed any offence.
He is innocent.
He has been falsely implicated.
He and prosecutrix both are major and they were having consensual sexual relationship.
Now relationship is not working, therefore, false case has been lodged.
Therefore, it is prayed that applicant may be released on bail.

sentences.text: On the other hand, learned counsel for the State as well as learned counsel for the objector have opposed the prayer for grant of bail to the applicant and has submitted that applicant has a criminal background of seven cases.
5 . Applicant has criminal background under M.P. Excise Act cases and this is the first case registered against the applicant under the provisions of IPC or BNSS, 2023.
Parties are major and near relatives.

Therefore, having taken into consideration all the facts and circumstances of the case,
but without expressing anything on the merits of the case, I am of the view that it is a case in which further pre trial detention of the applicant is not warranted.

Consequently, this bail application under Section 483 of BNSS, 2023/439 of Cr.P.C., 1973 for grant of bail filed on behalf of applicant,
stands allowed.

6 . It is directed that applicant - Trilochan Singh be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty thousand only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court, for his regular appearance before the trial Court during trial with a condition that he shall remain present before the concerned Court on all the dates fixed by it during trial.

He shall abide by all the conditions enumerated under Section 437(3) of Cr.P.C.,
1973 [Section 480(3) of BNSS, NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:17279 3 MCRC-11885-2025 2023].
7 .
This order shall be effective till the end of the trial.
However, in case of bail jump and breach of any of the conditions of bail, it shall become ineffective.
Certified copy as per rules.

(DINESH KUMAR PALIWAL) JUDGE Jasleend Trilochan Singh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 9 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/45757610/
